data.why: Public tournament catalogue; readable by design.

blast.why: Global; a tournament row governs a competition many accounts enter.

integrity.why: EVIDENCE CORRECTION (was High by analogy). Traced: the entry fee is debited as `-SPRINT.entryFee` (create-session/index.ts:1611) and prizes credited as `placement.prizeChips` derived from `SPRINT.prizeChips` (tournament-format.ts:44,295) — both CODE-side constants. The tournaments row's entry_fee_chips, starting_chips and prize_structure are WRITTEN from those constants at creation (index.ts:1472-1480) and never read back to move chips. Independent validation: public.sprint_format() returns the figures as SQL literals and supabase/tests/16_sprint_and_daily.test.sql asserts it agrees field by field with the TypeScript constant, so neither money path reads this mutable row.

data.why: Broadcast transport carrying sanitised PublicGameState and presence. The payload withholds the hole card and future shoe order by construction.

blast.why: A game topic reaches that session's seated participants; the presence topic is one shared roster.

integrity.why: A client writing to a game topic can push a fabricated table onto other players' screens — Arc21 measured exactly this before the policies existed. It corrupts shared non-authoritative behaviour; the server's state is unaffected.

reversibility.why: Transport, not a record. public.game_events is described in the broadcast module as the durable ordered record a client falls back to, so a lost or corrupted message has an authoritative source to recover from.

exposure.why: Author's decision: effective current exposure is authenticated. All three policies name `authenticated`; the anonymous table grant exists beneath them but matches no applicable policy, and is recorded as defence-in-depth context rather than current reachability.
